title: The Human Conversion Imperative: Machine Acceleration, Human Potential, and the Reversibility Window in an AI-Robotic World

equations.meaning: The joint problem generated by When AI Expands Human Potential and After Labour: machine capability growth does not entail human capability growth; the missing dependent variable is the rate/direction of conversion.
First of the explicit separations opening the non-collapse discipline.
Non-collapse: performance while assisted by AI is not the same object as durable human learning.
Non-collapse: human+AI outperforming human alone (augmentation) is not the same as outperforming the better of human or AI alone (synergy).
Non-collapse: legally/formally available options are not the same as practically live possibilities.
Non-collapse: having access to a gate is not the same as having a credible substitute/exit from it.
Non-collapse: a current income transfer does not by itself build future ownership.
Non-collapse: being materially secure is not the same as having agency.
Non-collapse: market concentration alone does not establish domination.
Non-collapse: humans may become less necessary to production while remaining socially necessary.

equations.section: 5. Human Conversion as a Vector, Not a Scalar
equations.text: C^H_t = < Gamma^eff_t, X^H_t, Lambda^live_(H,t), A^corr_(H,t), R^route_(H,t), W^world_(H,t), r_(H,t), H^cap_t, S_(H,t) >
equations.meaning: Human Conversion Vector: effective material claim, credible exit, live possibility, corrigible agency, independent epistemic routes, world-answerability, delayed unaided Human Return, social-reproductive capability, and recognized standing.

equations.section: 5. Human Conversion as a Vector, Not a Scalar
equations.meaning: Local Human Conversion Elasticity for dimension j against a declared machine-capability measure M_t.

equations.section: 5. Human Conversion as a Vector, Not a Scalar
equations.meaning: A mixed trajectory permitted by the vector framing: machine capacity can raise material consumption while reducing retained human competence and exit, which one positive 'augmentation' score would conceal.

equations.label: Proposition 1
equations.section: 5. Human Conversion as a Vector, Not a Scalar
equations.text: Proposition 1 (Conversion non-identity) [Open]. An increase in M_t or current human-AI performance is insufficient to establish human expansion unless at least one predeclared Human Conversion dimension improves without unacceptable deterioration in another load-bearing dimension.
equations.meaning: Boxed proposition guarding against inferring human expansion from machine-capability or performance growth alone.

equations.text: H problem -> AI divergence -> H resistance -> World test -> H integration -> AI removal -> H return
equations.meaning: The form of a high-conversion human-AI interaction, inheriting the closure/corrigibility distinction from When AI Expands Human Potential.

equations.text: H problem -> AI answer -> use -> dependence
equations.meaning: The form of a low-conversion interaction: systems optimized only for short-run completion can substitute for the cognitive work needed to build future independent competence.

equations.label: Proposition 2
equations.text: Proposition 2 (Assistance-conversion divergence) [Open]. The AI assistance intensity that maximizes current performance need not maximize delayed Human Return or corrigible agency.
equations.meaning: Boxed proposition separating the assistance level that maximizes current performance from the one that maximizes durable conversion.

equations.section: 7. Bad Mode Is a State Space, Not a Staircase
equations.text: B_t = < D_t, G_dot^conv_t, C^info_t, 1 - X^H_t, 1 - r_(H,t), 1 - Lambda^live_(H,t), 1 - A^corr_(H,t), 1 - Gamma^eff_t, 1 - H^cap_t >
equations.meaning: Bad-Mode State Vector: dependency, conversion-gate power, informational concentration, and the shortfalls of exit, Human Return, live possibility, corrigible agency, effective claim, and human-capability stock; a 'bad mode' is a sustained trajectory, not a fixed threshold.

equations.section: 8. Reversibility, Hysteresis, and the Intervention Window
equations.text: W_j = { t : C^rec_(j,t) <= C_bar_j  AND  tau^rec_(j,t) <= tau_bar_j }
equations.meaning: Reversibility Window: the set of times for which restoration of dimension j remains feasible under declared recovery-cost and recovery-time bounds.

equations.label: Proposition 3
equations.section: 8. Reversibility, Hysteresis, and the Intervention Window
equations.text: Proposition 3 (Reversibility Principle) [Open]. The faster machine capability grows relative to human conversion, the more valuable it becomes to preserve reversible human and institutional alternatives before the recovery cost of lost routes rises.
equations.meaning: Boxed reversibility principle: urgency of preserving reversibility rises with the growth gap between machine capability and human conversion.

equations.section: 9. An Urgency Vector Instead of a Panic Index
equations.meaning: Conversion-gap term: the positive part of the difference between normalized machine growth and human-conversion-dimension growth.

equations.section: 9. An Urgency Vector Instead of a Panic Index
equations.text: U_(j,t) = Delta g_(j,t) * L_(j,t) * S_(j,t) * tau^rec_(j,t)
equations.meaning: Urgency term for dimension j, combining the machine/human growth gap with lock-in intensity, severity, and expected recovery time.

equations.section: 9. An Urgency Vector Instead of a Panic Index
equations.meaning: The Urgency Vector collecting per-dimension urgency terms.

equations.section: 9. An Urgency Vector Instead of a Panic Index
equations.meaning: A bottleneck summary preventing severe deterioration in one dimension from being averaged away by gains elsewhere; a weighted average is permitted only with explicit normative weights.
Distributional readouts for any Human Conversion dimension: 10th, 50th, and 90th percentiles across the population.
A simple spread measure of distributional inequality in conversion; a rising mean is not maximum human potential if the majority becomes more dependent.

equations.label: Proposition 4
equations.text: Proposition 4 (Distributional conversion) [Open]. Broad human expansion requires that conversion gains reach a declared population distribution; aggregate productivity or mean capability gains are insufficient.
equations.meaning: Boxed proposition requiring conversion gains to be evaluated across the population distribution, not only the mean.

equations.section: 15. Discussion: From Maximum Assistance to Maximum Conversion
equations.text: Maximum AI assistance -> Maximum durable human conversion
equations.meaning: The design-objective shift the framework proposes: from maximizing assisted performance to maximizing the quality of the human state that emerges after assistance.

equations.text: rate of machine capability growth  versus  rate of human conversion and institutional adaptation
equations.meaning: The defining race of an AI-robotic century, framed as two competing rates rather than human intelligence versus machine intelligence.

equations.text: Machine Capability -> Human Conversion Vector -> Human Return/Agency/Exit -> Reversibility or Lock-in -> Next Institutional State
equations.meaning: The compressed architecture summarizing the Human Conversion Imperative as a design principle.
